text:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to lock scope for the 'tenant-priority lanes' customer pilot. Asking runtime/infra/security + QA for alignment by EOD Fri. TL;DR: product wants per-tenant priority routing + billing attribution + graceful fallback to default lane. This needs to be safe for pilot customers and reversible.

Devon: Can you list the exact runtime/infrastructure asks? Is this header metadata + KV tag only or are we touching model variants/quantization?

Maya: Good q — minimal product asks: 1) request carries a tenant_priority token (enum: high, normal), 2) router should prefer priority pool for high, 3) emit billing tag and tenant-id in traces, 4) fallback rules if priority pool at capacity. No model architecture changes expected for pilot.

Ash: Runtime notes: we'll need tag-aware KV cache and router aware of priority buckets. Also continuous-batching logic must preserve priority order (can't starve normal). Estimate: prototype for pilot = ~2 dev sprints (one focused on routing + cache tagging, second on rollout hardening). Need kernel perf check for extra KV metadata and memory impact.

Liam: Infra: we can carve out reserved capacity for the pilot (suggest 8 GPUs across 2 pools to simulate pressure). Need a short-term commit for reservations (30d). I'll draft cost and slot sizing once we lock expected qps. Also need network policies for tenant isolation and labels for billing.

Priya: Security: requirements include a dataflow diagram, threat model for tenant tagging leakage, KMS plan for any tenant-specific keys, and acceptance criteria for the pilot (no cross-tenant data in logs). If we scope pilot to non-PII customers we can accelerate signoff. SOC checklist + pen test scheduling will still be required before GA.

Devon: If we pick the "logical isolation + KMS scoping" approach (product rec), runtime work is limited to tagging, router policy, and emitting audit events. We can do feature-flag rollout and circuit-breaker for capacity falls. Who owns end-to-end tests?

Sasha: QA here — I can own e2e/perf test harness. Need a test-tenant generator and test flag. ETA to produce smoke + perf suites: 1 week after runtime prototype branch is ready. Will also add chaos scenarios for fallback behavior.

Maya: Decision options for exec:
A) Full isolation (per-tenant keys + dedicated VPCs) = high effort, strong compliance.
B) Logical isolation (tagging + KMS scoping + infra labels) = medium effort, acceptable for pilot.
C) Soft isolation (app-only tagging) = low effort, NOT acceptable for regulated customers.

Product recommendation: B for pilot (faster, gives auditability).

Maya: Action items (owners & rough dates):
- @Ash: prototype tag-augmented KV cache + router changes by Wed (3623456880).
- @Liam: draft reservation terraform + cost estimate by Thu EOD.
- @Priya: start threat model doc & list required artifacts by Thu.
- @Sasha: test plan + tenant generator ready by Thu EOD.
I'll take this to exec Fri 10am to lock final scope. Please flag blockers here ASAP. :calendar:

Devon: +1. A couple notes: we'll need a canary policy for latency-sensitive customers and a fast rollback path. Also confirm metrics we need to monitor (p50/p95 latency per lane, tail token cost, cache hit rate by tenant).

Ash: noted — will add metrics hooks and a `priority_fallback` gauge. Also will add a config toggle to revert to default router behavior.

Liam: draft reservation snippet (provisional):
```hcl
resource "redwood_compute_reservation" "tenant_prio_pilot" {
  gpus = 8
  label = "tenant-prio-pilot"
  duration = "30d"
}
```
I'll post numbers in the cost doc.

Priya: I'll start the threat model and ping legal for consent language if we think we'll touch any sensitive logs. If product limits pilot to non-sensitive tenants, we can probably get security signoff faster.

DeployBot: Heads-up — scheduled infra maintenance Wed 02:00-04:00 UTC may affect reservation test runs.

Maya: Thanks all. If no major blockers, we'll proceed with plan B and reconvene Thu morning for a quick status check.
